recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-6149; any future grammar cleanup in the Bundle transaction paragraph should be handled as a separate editorial issue.
issue_request: FHIR-6149 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 technical correction for the Bundle transaction narrative. It reported that the sentence 'Each entry element MAY contain a transaction element, and MAY contain either a resource element' was incomplete after 'either' and asked for the text to be corrected.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 5354, which corresponds to git commit 12427be0018a72ecad38f4aa697d9660278a2ca7. That commit changed the sentence to say each transaction entry SHALL contain either a transaction element or a resource element, or both, and retained the PUT/POST resource body rule.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini. Later final issues in the same Bundle transaction family replaced obsolete transaction-element terminology with Bundle.entry.request, made request details mandatory for transaction and batch entries, clarified matching HTTP prose, removed the old either/or sentence, and preserved the rule in invariant bdl-3c. Existing combined-branch audit commits already represent FHIR-8874, FHIR-8881, FHIR-14550, FHIR-14551, FHIR-17083, and FHIR-38942.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Bundle narrative says transaction/batch entries contain a request element with HTTP operation details and contain a resource for PUT, PATCH, or POST, while bdl-3c enforces request.method and the same resource condition. Reintroducing the old either/or wording would conflict with later approved request-based rules.

related_jiras.note: Replaced non-existent Bundle transaction-element wording with request-element wording in the same narrative family; already audited on the combined branch.
Clarified whether request is compulsory in transaction Bundle entries; already audited on the combined branch.
Targeted punctuation in the later either-or request/resource sentence and records that the text had gone; already audited on the combined branch.
Made Bundle.entry.request mandatory for transaction and batch bundles, superseding the original optional/either-or framing.
Clarified the matching HTTP transaction prose to say each entry SHALL carry request details.
Moved redundant SHALL prose into Bundle invariants, including bdl-3c for transaction/batch request and resource requirements.
